_comment: How a player's body build is chosen, from position, height and weight only.
The save stores it in the Player table's CharacterBodyType column, as one of
five strings. 'Freshman' is the stored name for the build the game's own
editor calls Lean — confirmed by a save in which five named Florida State
players were given each build in turn and read back out.
Two sources, and they answer different questions.
builder  — EA's own player builder: which builds a given height and weight
can carry at all. Supplied by the project owner from the game's
editor. This is what keeps a 175 lb receiver from being written
as Muscular.
One deliberate departure from the source table: the Lean band.
The builder's own cutoff rises with height, from 175 lb at 5'9"
to 210 lb at 6'5", before Standard becomes available; the
game's own rosters carry Standard players down to 160 lb at
every height. It is set to a flat 170 here. Chosen rather than
measured, and it moved agreement with the game from 76.5% to
82.6% against an 86.8% ceiling.
positions — what the game itself puts on each position, measured across the
16,257 players of a base save (tools/measure_body_types.py).
Every 'always' entry below is the position's own modal build,
and matching it exactly reproduces the best any rule reading
position, height and weight could do for that position.
Positions the builder gates choose among the light builds it permits. The
'always' positions do not consult it at all: the table describes the light
builds, and its 'Standard/Thin only' band below 220 lb would make a 215 lb
linebacker a Standard build the game itself never uses. Gating them costs
six points of agreement and buys nothing — a 300 lb guard's build was never
in question.
Keyed by height in inches. 69 covers anything shorter; 77 is the table's
'>6 4"' row and covers anything taller. Bands are tried in order and the
first one containing the weight wins, so the boundary weights the source
table repeats (6'3" 220, 6'2" 240) resolve to the earlier, wider band.
